# AI Media Scout — 2026-11-26

The edition has 122 complete guides and 10 screened discoveries. It completes 29 earlier pending guides and details 2 substantive release updates. This edition follows local interview review on Windows and macOS, reference color across shots, editable drum notation and model-assisted tape restoration. The application, weights and media limits are recorded per workflow. Scarlet fixes speaker attribution during transcript corrections and adds a recovery route for export. LocalSR fixes output timestamps and launch issues on macOS 14 and 15. Godot extensions cover live transcription and baked mouth cues. AutoAOV offers per-pass neural denoising with documented limits on depth and motion data. A GitLab transcription prototype and an earlier SourceHut diffusion runner show how hosted recognition and local build dependencies affect the available workflow. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 63 fields, 399/399 repository-query attempts and 23 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 398 successful, 1 partial and 0 failed queries, with 99 bounded. The model lane recorded 0 failed tasks. Metadata from 533 saved repository pages included 19,204 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 125,439 candidates, including pilot history and 1,062 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. Live primary research yielded 471 complete usable responses from 567 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 63 fields. 3 captures reached the size bound and 93 other sources were inaccessible or unusable. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 118 Quality unverified, 14 Experimental. Independent use remains unverified for 129 entries. The creative result check remains unverified for 130, and model, service or cost requirements remain unverified for 132. Repository searches returned no saved rows for Learned film, tape and audio restoration, Embodied and tactile interactive art, Multiband art and heritage imaging, Narrated and tactile exhibition interfaces, Learned shot matching and grading. Primary web research for these fields is included in the coverage notes. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: Diffuser (SourceHut) (Quality unverified to Experimental), Arabic Calligraphy for AI Agents (Quality unverified to Experimental), Arclight (Quality unverified to Experimental). 23 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. All saved model-task results were screened as metadata, covering 1,150 rows and 1,150 distinct model identities. The two linked source guides for the vocal denoiser and RCDL have separately verified software grants. The separate watchlist made 69 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 1 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Documentation reviewed today. Tools are not hands-on tested unless explicitly stated. Requirements and performance remain source-specific.

Rehearse direct hand control of an editable object layout, using original or licensed GLB assets and a recoverable manual control route. [Source 1](https://github.com/yc9954/motioncad/blob/main/README.md)

### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/yc9954/motioncad/blob/main/README.md)

3. Save the scene and record when a lost hand or fast gesture breaks the mapping.

[Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

### What it is good for

Index a copy of a mobile shoot and compare local group suggestions while preserving original files and managing your own backup bucket. [Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

### Demo & examples

The publisher documents on-device people groups, a visible original/edited comparison and a separate checksum-verified upload step. [Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

### Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

1. Review the documented Flutter development and personal deployment requirements.
2. Set up your own scoped Google Cloud Storage bucket and Firebase configuration for the documented backup path.
3. Choose a compatible licensed MobileFaceNet model only if embedding-based grouping is needed.
### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

1. Import a short authorization-cleared project folder, leaving any optional offload setting disabled for the review.
2. Check face-group assignments manually and confirm which steps use Google services.
3. Verify downloaded copies and keep your original sources before changing any storage policy.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/veluralabs/nimbus/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veluralabs/nimbus/main/assets/models/README.md)

- **Hardware:** Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk space for the scoped workflow are undocumented.
- **Software:** Flutter, Firebase Auth and Google Cloud Storage. The local model route lists a compatible MobileFaceNet TFLite file. Vertex AI is a separate optional editing service.
- **Platforms:** The maintainer lists Android 8.0/API 26+ and iOS 13+. The iOS build route documents Xcode 15 and a signing identity.

[Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

### What it is good for

Build an editable arrangement sketch from a short original lyric or voice note. Keep words, generated takes and the selected stems independently editable. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

### Demo & examples

Publisher workflows show tracking an original prompt through alternate takes, vocal and instrumental stems, Basic Pitch conversion and REAPER project output. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

### Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

1. Review the documented client and ACE-Step setup and configure one compatible model endpoint.
2. Select the Whisper/FFmpeg path and add only the optional stem and MIDI tools required for an editable handoff.
### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

1. Provide an original lyric or permission-cleared voice note and inspect the transcribed words.
2. Generate a short alternate take and choose the phrasing that fits the brief.
3. Compare each stem and imported MIDI against the source and audition the assembled project in its downstream editor.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

- **Hardware:** The maintainer states approximately 8 GB VRAM for the turbo model, with slower CPU fallback. Different ACE-Step variants have separate requirements.
- **Software:** BosonSong CLI or documented Claude Code integration, ACE-Step v1.5, faster-whisper and FFmpeg. Demucs, Basic Pitch and REAPER are separate optional paths.
- **Platforms:** Publisher gives platform-specific component guidance, including FFmpeg packages for Linux and macOS. A full supported app/platform matrix is undocumented.

### License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/LICENSE) [Source 2](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

- **Code:** MIT
- **Weights:** MIT integration. ACE-Step models, speech transcription, stem separation, MIDI tools, REAPER and submitted references have independent terms.
- **Commercial:** Project code is governed by MIT. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
- **Cost:** Local GPU time, model storage and optional agent or hosted GPU access.

### Why it merits attention

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

### Limitations

A generated take and its separated stems can contain artifacts. The documented add-track workflows require a separate base model configuration. [Source 1](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5)

### Get the tool

- [Repository](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong)
- [Documentation](https://github.com/bosons14/bosonsong/blob/main/README.md)

## Scarlet

Compared with v0.1.539, v0.1.576 keeps corrected transcript words with the speaker who said them, retains a chosen voice track and volume changes during specified dialogue edits, and retries a timeline or caption export after an engine restart. Confirmed against the two tagged changelogs and the changed source tree.

### Quality assessment: Experimental

Creative use and the code grant are documented. Check-level gaps remain before a recommendation.

Scope: Work through a dialogue-driven interview cut, including a correction across adjacent speakers followed by a caption or timeline handoff.

Evidence checked: 2026-11-26. No local execution implied.

Why Experimental: The current maintainer README describes active early development. Desktop packages still have signing limitations, and the Linux route remains a separate preview. https://github.com/Forward-Future/scarlet/blob/main/README.md

The motion-net package supplies a browser/WASM runtime for a neural motion codebook that can contribute gait to a three.js character. Related packages provide conventional rigging and retargeting. ### What it is good for

Use an editable browser rig to compare a neural gait with a known rehearsal motion and diagnose root or foot-contact changes. [Source 1](https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-motion/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/)

The publisher provides separate package example pages and an automated browser check report that discloses which combinations were skipped. [Source 1](https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-motion/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/)

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-motion/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-motion/)

### How it uses AI

### MIDI Velocity Colorizer · CC0-1.0

### SRswift · CC0-1.0

Use an editable rule pipeline to place a label or exhibit object near a tracked scene feature in an AR experience.
The Swift symbolic inference engine derives spatial relationships from an object fact base. An authored rule can choose or produce interactive AR objects based on relationships in a scene.
Reviewed the complete CC0 software dedication and the author’s inference syntax. A guide needs release-specific build and scene integration steps, supported Apple device evidence and independently verified output.
